title: Module localization is the filtered colimit over powers
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, f an element of A, and M an A-module. The canonical map from the filtered colimit of the directed system M \xrightarrow{f} M \xrightarrow{f} M with every transition multiplication by f to the localization M_f [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away] is an isomorphism of A-modules; the class of m at stage e maps to m/f^e.

source.place: Tag 00CM, module localization as a colimit

proof.text: Index the copies of $M$ by the ordered set of natural numbers, with the transition from stage $e$ to stage $e+1$ equal to multiplication by $f$. This is a filtered category: it is nonempty, any two stages have a common later stage, and a poset has no distinct parallel arrows. For each $e$ define $\kappa_e:M\to M_f$ by $\kappa_e(m)=m/f^e$. These maps are $A$-linear and compatible, since $\kappa_{e+1}(fm)=fm/f^{e+1}=m/f^e$. Thus the universal property of the colimit gives a canonical $A$-linear map $\kappa:\varinjlim_eM\to M_f$.

source.place: Tag 00CM, module localization as a colimit

proof.text: The map kappa is surjective. Every element of M_f is a fraction m/f^e by the definition of localization at the powers of f, and this is kappa applied to the class of m at stage e.

source.place: Tag 00CM, module localization as a colimit

proof.text: The map kappa is injective. Suppose the classes of m at stage e and n at stage d have the same image. By the equality criterion in the localization, there is a natural number r such that f^r(f^d m-f^e n)=0. Set E=e+d+r. After transporting both representatives to stage E, their difference is f^{E-e}m-f^{E-d}n=f^r(f^d m-f^e n)=0. The equality criterion for elements in a filtered colimit of modules therefore says that the two classes in colim_e M are equal.

source.place: Tag 00CM, module localization as a colimit

proof.text: The canonical map kappa is both A-linear and bijective, so it is an isomorphism of A-modules, with the stated formula on the class of m at stage e.
